messages.content:
Three independent readers read the same non-disclosure agreement (NDA) and decided whether it supports one statement (the hypothesis). They may agree or disagree, and a program has checked each of their quotes against the document. Your job is to make the final decision yourself, from the document.

<document>
<document 482 omitted, sha256 80794af356908844>
</document>

<hypothesis>
Confidential Information shall only include technical information.
</hypothesis>

<readings>
<reading id="A">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 92
reason: The NDA defines Confidential Information broadly, and the recitals list technical data, marketing, business information, and pricing, so it is not limited to technical information.
<quote check="exact">all information provided orally by a Party which that Party desires to protect from disclosure</quote>
<quote check="exact">technical data, marketing, business information, and pricing</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="B">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 88
reason: The agreement covers business, marketing and pricing information as well as technical data, and defines Confidential Information as all information marked as confidential, so it is not limited to technical information.
<quote check="exact">relating, but not limited, to technical data, marketing, business information, and pricing</quote>
<quote check="exact">disclose to the other Party certain technical or business information</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="C">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 90
reason: The definition covers all marked information, and the agreement expressly contemplates business, marketing and pricing information, not only technical information.
<quote check="exact">"Confidential Information" means all information provided by either Party in writing or visual form which Party desires to protect from disclosure</quote>
<quote check="exact">technical data, marketing, business information, and pricing</quote>
<quote check="exact">disclose to the other Party certain technical or business information</quote>
</reading>
</readings>

The readings are evidence about where to look, not votes: a majority can be wrong, and a quote marked "missing" was not found in the document. Read the relevant parts of the document yourself.

Choose exactly one label:
- Entailment: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is true.
- Contradiction: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is false.
- NotMentioned: the document does not address the hypothesis, or says too little to decide.

Evidence is required. For Entailment or Contradiction, give 1 to 3 quotes copied character for character from the document (no paraphrase, no ellipses), each as short as it can be while still carrying the point. They will be checked against the document. For NotMentioned, give an empty list.

Give a confidence from 0 to 100: your probability, in percent, that your label is correct. Give a one-sentence reason.

Answer only with the JSON object the response format asks for: label, confidence, quotes, reason.

content.text: {"label":"Contradiction","confidence":92,"quotes":["\"Confidential Information\" means all information provided by either Party in writing or visual form","technical data, marketing, business information, and pricing","disclose to the other Party certain technical or business information"],"reason":"Confidential Information is defined as all marked or confirmed information, and the agreement expressly covers business, marketing and pricing information, so it is not limited to technical information."}
